priority-inversion-1.text:
CAUSE: The mutex at 0x1c40854040 was held by brakesim/logger (priority 10) while brakesim/brake_ctl (priority 63) attempted to lock it, causing brake_ctl to block in the MUTEX state. Because the mutex did not employ priority inheritance or priority protection, logger remained at priority 10 and was preempted by brakesim/telemetry (priority 30), which ran for 72.9 ms while logger was ready but not running. This prevented logger from releasing the mutex, forcing brake_ctl to wait 74.4 ms and resulting in a worst-case priority inversion of 72.9 ms.
FIX: Change the mutex creation attributes for 0x1c40854040 to use PTHREAD_PRIO_INHERIT or PTHREAD_PRIO_PROTECT so that the logger thread's priority is temporarily raised to match the highest-priority waiting thread (brake_ctl) while it holds the lock. This will ensure logger preempts telemetry and releases the mutex promptly, eliminating the inversion.

deadline-miss-1.text:
CAUSE: The `brakesim/brake_ctl` thread (priority 63) was blocked for 74.4 ms waiting to acquire a mutex held by the low-priority `brakesim/logger` thread (priority 10). Because the mutex does not appear to be using priority inheritance, the logger continued to run at its base priority of 10, preventing the higher-priority brake controller from executing until the logger voluntarily released the lock. This caused the worst-case response time to reach 75.4 ms, significantly exceeding the 15.0 ms deadline.
FIX: Change the mutex creation attributes to use `PTHREAD_PRIO_INHERIT` so that the `brakesim/logger` thread temporarily inherits the priority of `brakesim/brake_ctl` while holding the lock. Alternatively, reduce the critical section length in the logger to minimize the blocking time for the real-time control thread.
